title: Lior and the Veil
premise: Quentin Reyes, the queen's food-taster, has spent years dosing herself with poison to survive court intrigue, and her knowledge of the Thornfell smuggler roads makes her the perfect courier when a dying stranger presses a bloodstained map into her hands. The map reveals the location of the Veilstone, an artifact whose theft decades ago erased an entire border people from living memory — and restoring it would reignite the war it once ended. Hunted by the crown's spymaster, who wants the stone destroyed to preserve a fragile peace, and shadowed by Sera, a woman who remembers fragments of the erased past, Quentin must choose between loyalty to the crown and justice for people no one remembers wronging. In the end she restores the memory of the lost rather than the stone itself, shattering the Veil's magic but sparing the war — at the cost of her own immunity-built identity and her place at court.
about_author: Theo Thackeray is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing disputed border treaties before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about the paperwork of empire and the people it forgets.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. A routine tasting at the royal table goes wrong when Quentin detects nightshade laced into the queen's wine, exposing a plot within the palace kitchens. Rewarded with suspicion rather than trust, she feels the walls of her gilded servitude closing in. Emotional beat: competence as captivity — Quentin is indispensable and utterly owned.

chapters.title: A Stranger at Thornfell Pass
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Sent to negotiate provisions with mountain smugglers, Quentin finds a dying man in a burned waystation who presses a leather map into her hands and gasps a name: 'the Veilstone.' Royal riders arrive hunting him; she hides the map and lies for the first time in her careful life. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration of the first transgression.

chapters.title: What the Map Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Studying the map in hiding, Quentin discovers roads on it that lead to villages she cannot find in any census — places that officially never existed. The spymaster, Lord Corvane, summons her for questioning about the dead stranger. Emotional beat: creeping dread as she realizes the erasure is bureaucratic, deliberate, total.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Half-Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Sera. A knife-sharp wanderer ambushes Quentin on the road, drawn by rumors of the map; she is a child of the erased Valeth people, carrying fragmented memories that shouldn't exist. Reluctant allies, they flee Corvane's hunters together through the smuggler roads only Quentin knows. Emotional beat: prickly distrust beginning to soften into necessity.

chapters.title: The Court of Smugglers
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Sheltering in a hidden freehold beneath Thornfell, Quentin and Sera barter passage with the smuggler queen Maren Voss, who knew the dying man. Maren reveals the Veilstone was stolen to end the last war by making both sides forget what they fought over. Emotional beat: found family flickering to life around a fire, fragile and conditional.

chapters.title: Corvane's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Captured by Corvane's agents, Quentin is offered amnesty and wealth if she surrenders the map; he shows her records proving the stone's restoration means war, famine, and the deaths of thousands. Released as a test of loyalty, she must decide what justice means when every option bleeds. Emotional beat: the weight of a choice with no clean side.

chapters.title: The Vale That Was
chapters.summary: POV Sera. Following the map's true route, Sera leads them into a valley that is physically present yet unseen — the erased Valeth homeland, still standing under the Veil's forgetting. She recovers memories of her mother among the empty houses. Emotional beat: grief made physical; Sera mourning a home she was robbed of remembering.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Freehold
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. One of Maren's crew sells their location to Corvane; the freehold burns, Maren falls covering their escape, and Quentin learns the dying stranger was her own estranged brother, who chose her deliberately. Emotional beat: rage and heartbreak — the cost of the secret becomes personal and irreversible.

chapters.title: The Veilstone
chapters.summary: POV Quentin and Sera alternating. At the vault beneath the Vale, Quentin holds the stone that can restore ten thousand erased lives — and Corvane arrives not with soldiers but with an honest plea: restore it and the old grievances return with the memories. Sera offers a third path: break the stone and let its power scatter into every mind in the realm. Emotional beat: the climax of conscience — justice outside the law, chosen at last.

chapters.title: Everything Remembered
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. The stone shatters; across the kingdom, people wake weeping over names they never knew, and the Valeth step back into history without a single sword drawn. Quentin, exposed as the taster who broke her oath, loses her place at court but gains a family — Sera, the freehold survivors, and a realm forced to reckon. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution; memory as both wound and homecoming.
